dish: the modern-classic French tasting menu (langoustine, Bresse pigeon)
w: Saarbrücken's temple of haute cuisine, in a Wilhelminian villa with its own park; a MICHELIN-Guide fixture (long a three-star, currently two) where Klaus Erfort serves an uncompromising, produce-driven classic French menu. The Saarland's flagship fine-dining address.

dish: the French-Japanese tasting menu (Bau's signature sashimi/sushi course, langoustine)
n: Victor's Fine Dining by Christian Bau
w: Germany's benchmark table right where Germany, France and Luxembourg meet, at Victor's Residenz-Schloss Berg. Christian Bau has held three MICHELIN stars uninterrupted since 2005 for a French haute cuisine fused early and brilliantly with Japanese product; ranked among the world's top ten on La Liste.

dish: Gefillde (stuffed potato dumplings) and the Saarland-Teller with house-brewed beer
w: Saarbrücken's oldest inn, on the St. Johanner Markt, brewing its own beer and plating the city's most robust Saarland cooking — Gefillde, the Saarland-Teller, hearty pub classics. The definitive place to eat the region's home kitchen in the capital.

A cosy family-run bistro in a lane off the St. Johanner Markt, run by the Grolier family for three decades, mixing German and French cooking and known for its own-made Dibbelabbes — the grated-potato hash that is one of Saarland's signature dishes.

dish: modern Saarland classics — Lyoner and 'Saarland tapas'
w: A younger address on Mainzer Straße giving Saarland cooking a modern turn — 'Saarland tapas', Lyoner, hearty classics reworked. A good hidden-gem counterpoint to the old brew-houses.

dish: the creative Lorraine tasting menu built on local produce
w: Metz's MICHELIN-starred table (starred since 2006), set inside the 1559 provisions store of the city's citadel at Hôtel La Citadelle. Chef Christophe Dufossé cooks refined, modern Lorraine cuisine anchored in regional produce.

dish: quiche lorraine and Lorraine bistro plates
w: A Parisian-style bistro in Metz's historic centre, 350 m from the cathedral, serving traditional French cooking with a Lorraine accent — quiche lorraine, home-style plates, regional wines by the pichet. Listed by the Inspire Metz tourist office and highly rated across platforms.

dish: Judd mat Gaardebounen (smoked pork collar with broad beans) and Gromperekichelcher
w: Probably the best-known address in the capital for genuine Luxembourgish home cooking, going 50 years — the national dish Judd mat Gaardebounen, Gromperekichelcher, Kniddelen — in a warm, rustic room in the heart of the Ville Haute.

dish: hand-made tortelli with parmesan and the eight-course Italian tasting menu
w: A MICHELIN-starred Italian jewel in the riverside Grund below the old town; chef Ilario Mosconi's Relais & Châteaux table (18/20 Gault&Millau) works imported Italian product into refined pasta and tasting menus overlooking the Alzette.

dish: Quetschentaart (plum tart) and the 1928 Rieslingspaschtéit (Riesling pâté)
w: A pâtisserie-traiteur institution on Place Guillaume II since 1922, keeper of Luxembourgish sweet-and-savoury tradition — the autumn Quetschentaart and the Rieslingspaschtéit created here in 1928 — alongside a deep cheese and fine-food counter.

dish: Luxembourg Crémant and Riesling tasting in the 1921 cellars
w: The visitor cellars of Luxembourg's biggest wine-and-crémant cooperative, on the Moselle bank at Grevenmacher and founded in 1921. Taste and buy the Grand Duchy's Riesling, Pinot and — above all — its sparkling Crémant de Luxembourg where the river marks the German border.

dish: Mosel Riesling by the glass from Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt with hearty regional plates
w: Trier's classic Weinstube, in the 250-year-old Palais Kesselstatt directly opposite the Liebfrauenkirche and cathedral, pouring Rieslings from the 650-year Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt estate's steep-slate Mosel/Saar/Ruwer sites alongside hearty regional cooking, self-serve at the counter. The signature Riesling-Weinstube experience of the Roman city.

dish: Bernkasteler Doctor Riesling with Mosel dishes (Moselforelle, Winzerbraten)
w: A half-timbered Weinstube in Bernkastel-Kues's fairy-tale old town, named for the world-famous Bernkasteler Doctor vineyard on the slate slope above it. The place to drink Middle-Mosel Riesling — the Doctor is one of Germany's most storied sites — with Mosel trout and vintner's roast.
